detail.title: Checkpoint publication reuses an existing content-addressed object without verifying its bytes

detail.reason:
Publication now verifies a content-addressed object against its own name before reusing it, at both write sites: publish_monolithic_checkpoint (root object) and write_content_object (sharded objects). An existing object is reused only when its sha256 still equals its name; on a mismatch the live serialization replaces the file atomically, the repair is named on stderr, and the repaired path lands in changed_paths so git staging picks up the fixed bytes. This un-sticks the observed state: with a hand-edited root, every later flush recomputed the identical address and republished the pointer against corrupt bytes, so status stayed 'root hash mismatch ... Ready to commit: NO' for 18 days.

Acceptance replayed end-to-end in tests/checkpoint_object_reuse_verification.rs: a byte-modified object planted at the exact address the next publication recomputes; flush-only exits 0 only after rewriting it, and sync status then shows root_verified=true, checkpoint_consistent=true with the mismatch reason gone; a second test pins that republication over unchanged state keeps a verified root reused byte-for-byte. Unit tests cover the sharded helper's write/reuse/repair trio and the monolith publisher's planted-address repair (forensic.jsonl view carries the repaired bytes).

Committed bf2aa10b, pushed to Forgejo origin/main; git rev-list origin/main..HEAD is empty. The definition of done ran in a git-archive extraction of HEAD at /var/tmp/dod-fb3100ce-hNqX: fmt + full test suite, 140 test-result lines, no failures. Only src/service/checkpoint.rs and tests/checkpoint_object_reuse_verification.rs were touched; other workers' staged checkpoint churn and dirty WIP were left as found.
